To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in papain-induced emphysema, the lung height-Ptp relationship is steeper and the gradient of transpulmonay pressure is greater than in normal dogs, and that during spontaneous breathing the vertical gradient of transpulongary pressure is greater in the head-up than in the supine posture.

in the supine posture the distribution of transpulmonay pressure ( Ptp ), at functional residual capacity ( FRC ) and during spontaneous breathing, is uniform in normal dogs but not in papain-treated emphysematious dogs.
the vertical gradient of lung Ptp at FCR is abolished in the head-up position of dogs with panlobular empysema, as in the normal dog, but that the horizontal gradient of Ptp is not abolished.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of panlobular pulmonary emphysema, induced experimentally in dogs by intratracheal injection of papain, on the distribution of Ptp at F.R.C., and of ventilation during quiet breathing.
the effects of panlobular (papain-induced) emphysema upon the distribution of transpulmonary pressure ( Ptp ), and upon the distribution of ventilation during spontaneous respiration.
the distribution of Ptp in the lung in normal and emphysematuous dogs in the horizontal postions and in normal and elderly man in the head-up position.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, although the distribution of Ptp is different in normal and in papain-treated lungs, the distribution of ventilation is not different.
papain emphysema is a model of panlobular disease in which the distribution of Ptp at FCR and of ventilation is similar to that in man with panlobular emphysema.

papain-induced emhysema is characterized by: ( a ) an increase in the vertical gradient of lung specific volumes, ( b ) a decrease in the vertical gradient in Ptp at Frc and during inflation of relaxed respiratory system, ( c ) an increase in vertical gradients of Ptp during spontaneous breathing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
papain-induced emphysema is associated with a steeper and shifted Ptp vs height relationship at FRC and a steeper slope of the P-V curve.

in papain-induced emphysema, in the horizontal postions, the distribution of Ptp and of ventilation are uniform in all regions of the lung; in the head-up position the distribution is more heterogeneous, with larger Ptp and ventilation values in the upper regions of the lung.

the vertical gradient in Ptp during inflation of the respiratory system is not affected by papain-induced panlobular emhysema, but the horizontal gradient in Ptp, which is absent in normal dogs, appears after papain injection, and the gradient in specific lung volume and ventilation is larger in papain-treated than in normal dogs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution of transpulmonay pressure is a useful index to evaluate the mechanical effects of emphysema and to assess the effects of postural change.

the distribution of Ptp in the lung is not a simple function of lung morphology and the shape of the lung, but is also influenced by the distribution of the pleural surface pressure, which in turn depends on the posture and on the presence or absence of lung lesions.
the distribution of pleuropulmonary pressure and of ventilation in the supine and lateral postures are similar in both normal and emphysematious dogs.
